title: マイクロ・ナノ加工
subtitle: Micro-Nano Processing
educationalGoal: Currently, technologies for realizing ultrafine parts and mechanisms are required for manufacturing, and these technologies are applied to pressure sensors, the heads of inkjet printers, MEMS such as gyroscopes, manufacture of Si-IC and LED substrates, and micro-machines. In addition, processing methods include not only top-down types that refine existing elements but bottom-up types that build up atoms according to the purpose. In this course, students will learn the basics of processing methods to obtain such ultrafine parts and mechanisms.
advice:
We will cover various leading-edge processes that can fabricate micro- to nanoscale parts. The outline of this class is shown below:
1. Relationship between the processing method and scale concepts expressed as micro, meso, and nano
2. Latest top-down micro-processing methods
3. Micro-processing using lasers
4. Planarization processing of Si wafers
5. Planarization processing using chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) methods
6. Outline of surface modification methods
7. Outline of MEMS
8. Summary
To deepen your understanding of the content of this course, exercise questions will be presented and explained appropriately. Students will need to bring a scientific calculator to class. In addition, special classes will be held for outside lecturers as needed.
requiredKnowledge: Fully understand related subjects as integrated research and development. Possess fundamental knowledge of elemental technology learned in processing-related subjects

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of dimensions expressed at the micro-, meso-, and nanoscales.
Be able to explain the principles and features of surface modification methods (PVD, CVD, etc.).
Be able to explain the characteristics and principles of ultraprecision polishing.
Be able to explain the processing principles and application examples of the latest micro-processing technology.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Explain the concept of dimensions expressed at the micro-, meso-, and nanoscales and the modification methods for material forming at these dimensions.
2. Explain surface modification methods and the functional thin film that they realize.
3. Explain the positioning and principles of ultraprecision polishing, the polishing conditions, and the method for selecting auxiliary materials consumed during its application.
4. Explain the latest processing methods and application examples that realize ultrafine dimensions.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Explain the concept of dimensions expressed at the micro-, meso-, and nanoscales.
2. Explain the principles of typical surface modification methods.
3. Explain the positioning and principles of ultraprecision polishing, and the method for selecting materials consumed during its application.
4. Explain the principles of the latest processing methods to realize shapes with extremely small dimensions.

lessons.content:
Use the syllabus to review the learning outline
and action goals of this course. It is necessary
 to understand which part of the educational
objectives of the department of mechanical
engineering is covered by this course, and also
to understand the standard of the concrete
achievement level.
Learn the basics of micro-processing and
learn the size concepts of the Micro-, Meso-
and Nano- scales.

Learn about ultra-precision machining
technology and its necessity (i.e.,
concepts of micro-cutting mechanisms,
problems in ultra-precision turning,
and influence of thermal deformation on
machining accuracy).

Learn about applications of micro-cutting
technology and peripheral technologies to
enable it (such as optical element dies,
micro-tools, processing devices, and
control).

Learn about micro-fabrication techniques using
high-energy beam machining (such as types
of lasers, processing principles, and
applications).

Learn the meaning and necessity of polishing pro
cesses. This includes studying general concepts
as well as ultra-precision cutting, grinding, an
d polishing.

Learn about lapping and polishing in abrasive
grain processing methods.

Test on the content of classes 1-6.

General Exercise: Case studies of micro-machinin
g technology used in various fields will
be introduced and future developments will be di
scussed.
